newsitem.title: GERMANY: NCA mulls extra Europe, US, SE Asia freighter flig.
newsitem.headline: NCA mulls extra Europe, US, SE Asia freighter flig.

text.p: Nippon Cargo Airlines said it is considering adding extra freighter flights from Japan to south-east Asia, Europe and the USA from this summer.
Eiji Tanaka, NCA vice-president sales and marketing, said delivery of an eighth Boeing 747-200F in August would allow four extra weekly freighter flights.
The new aircraft will be the first of two converted B747-200 passenger aircraft from sister airline All Nippon Airways, with the second due for delivery in 1998.

Tanaka said the Japanese cargo airline currently operates 31 freighter flights a week, with 13 departures each for the U.S. and south-east Asia and five to Amsterdam, with two of these flights extended to Milan.
"We would like to increase to one more flight from Japan to the U.S., one more to Europe and two to South-East Asia," he told Reuters.
But he declined to say which destinations were under consideration at present and stressed no final decisions had yet been made.
Tanaka was speaking following the signing of a ground handling contract with trucking company Rutges BV at Frankfurt airport.
He added: "We would like to fly to Frankfurt but we need German governmental approval for that. Until then, we have to develop our business other ways."
There were no signs that NCA was likely to get Frankfurt landing rights in the near future, he pointed out.
NCA was enjoying double-digit growth from Germany, Tanaka noted.

Shigejiro Isogai, NCA general manager Europe, said that Germany provided most freight on the ex-Europe freighters followed by Benlux and Italy, with relatively little cargo coming from Britain, Scandinavia or France.
Ex-Europe business was a little weaker in 1996 than 1995 but had remained stable, he added.
Akira Todori, NCA regional manager for central and eastern Europe, said the airline currently trucked 700 tonnes a month from Germany to Amsterdam.
Ex-Germany tonnage in 1996 had been stable compared to 1995 and was in any case limited by a fixed allotment system, he added. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
